## 2026-11-11 - Planet environments: volcanic heat, slippery ice
- Asked: volcanic planets slow health regeneration by 50%, ice planets slow movement speed by 20%.
- Planets.ENVIRONMENT (planet_data.gd), by tile set: "vo" regen 0.5 (the heat), "ic" speed 0.8 (slippery
  ice); Planets.environment(id) merges a planet's own "environment" entry over its set's. The pilot gets
  regen_mult and speed (Pilot.SPEED 190 px/s x the planet's) as the surface makes it; regeneration is
  REGEN (6/s, after 4 s out of the fight) x regen_mult - 3/s on Akrotiri; walking 152 px/s on Ida and Kamares.
  On landing the event log says so ("The heat: your health comes back half as fast." / "Slippery ice: you
  walk 20% slower.").
- Docs: game.md (Akrotiri's heat; ice). Test: test_volcanic.test_environments (the table; on Akrotiri, Ida

## 2026-11-11 - Gear: equipment for the ship and the automaton
- Asked: item slots for spaceships and the automaton, giving passive effects, weapons and weapon modifiers that
  enhance health, damage, resistance etc.; bought at stations, dropped by NPCs, rewarded in encounters. Chosen
  (asked): merge with the outfitting modules into one system; a fixed catalogue with quality E-A; damage types
  with resistances; the full 7-slot loadout on foot.
- Gear (scripts/gear.gd, new): items "gear:<kind>:<quality>" (E Common, D Fine, C Superior, B Rare,
  A Masterwork - effects x1 / 1.3 / 1.65 / 2.05 / 2.5, weapon damage x1-1.6, price x1-26; sold at 60%).
  Ship gear = Shipyard.MODULES (the 7 old modules + Focusing Lens, Capacitor Bank, Targeting Computer (weapon
  modifiers), Ablative Plating, Reactive Armour, Heat Shield, Cryo Baffles (resistances), Nanite Repair
  (passive)) - fitted ones stay the player's `modules`; Gear.fit / unfit move them to and from the hold.
  Automaton gear = Gear.FOOT: 5 weapons (Laser Rifle - the default, E -, Pulse Carbine, Plasma Rifle (heat),
  Rail Rifle (kinetic), Cryo Rifle (cold)), 4 weapon mods, 4 armours, 3 cores, 5 passives; the loadout (weapon,
  mod1, mod2, armour, core, passive1, passive2) saved as the player's "loadout".
- Damage types (energy, kinetic, explosive, heat, cold): Ship.take_damage / Pilot.surface_hit take a dtype
  (default kinetic); resistance "resist_<type>" from gear and tech, capped at 75%. Lasers / bolts / beams /
  anomalies energy, plasma and fire breath heat, missiles explosive, frost orbs cold, bites and rams kinetic
  (the volcanic beasts' bites heat). Heat resistance eases Akrotiri's healing penalty, cold the ice's slowness.
- The automaton's stats (Pilot.apply_gear): damage / rate / reach / type / bolt colour from the weapon and mods,
  health, resistances, healing, speed, overcharge length - re-applied when the loadout changes.
- Sources: the Outfitting tab (one quality selector for the page - five price buttons on every row was 180
  buttons; ship gear fits at once or goes to the hold; automaton gear to the hold; fitted modules can go to
  the hold); destroyed ships 12% (+25% with toughness; bosses' level 1); pirates 15%, big beasts 10% (volcanic
  15%), chests 20%, lockers 25%, vaults 60%; every completed signal source (quality by level, 2 from insane).
- UI: LoadoutPanel (new) in the Ship Computer's inventory (from the hold) and the Field Computer's (from what
  you carry) - drag or click to equip, right-click to take off, a stats line; the Ship Computer's Ship Gear row
  (fitted modules; drag / click to fit, right-click to take out). Items.info / Items.exists: gear in every
  inventory, the sell list, icons (a glyph per slot in a ring of the quality's colour).
- Docs: game.md (Gear; Outfitting). Tests: tests/test_gear.gd (5: catalogue and items, equipping, the
  automaton's stats and resistances and the environment, the surface, ship gear and resistance, saving).
  179 tests pass. Frame rate: not re-measured - another game was using ~5 cores (the Outfitting tab went
  from 175 to 302 FPS with the quality selector even so); re-run tools/fps_test.py on an idle machine.

## 2026-11-11 - Published patches join the open version automatically
Asked: "make them go automatically" (unpublished patches should go to version 0.2).
Done: tools/patch.py gained `open_version()` (the version file with "open": true, else the newest)
and `assign_to_version(id)`, called first in `baseline <id>`: the patch id goes into the version's
`patches`, a page is added (title "Patch <id> - <title>", the summary's first two sentences, a
diagram of the patch's title box + up to 6 step badges) and a sentence to the version summary.

"open": true. CLAUDE.md's versions paragraph documents it.

## 2026-11-11 - Solar systems of 1 to 12 planets, of the four types, some with moons
Asked: "a solar system can have from 1 to 12 planets, pick from the 4 types we have already defined, some planets have moons".
Done:
- Galaxy._generate_planets: every generated system (all but Knossos) gets 1-12 planets (was 2-5 purely
  cosmetic, unlandable ones from 7 templates). Type by distance from the star (Galaxy._planet_type):
  inner third mostly volcanic, middle mostly ocean, outer ice and gas giants. Moons: chance by type
  (gas giant 85%, 1-3 moons; ocean 35%, ice 30%, volcanic 15%: one) - Kamares's kind (barren, grey),
  named "<planet> I/II/III". Orbits are spaced by each planet's size and its moons' orbits; the gates
  move out beyond the outermost planet when the system is bigger than the old 11000 radius.
- Planets.TYPES (ocean -> Amnissos, ice -> Ida, volcanic -> Akrotiri, gas giant -> Dikte, moon -> Kamares)
  and Planets.get_planet(id) for generated ids ("<system>_p<n>", moons "...m<k>"): the type's surface
  (terrain, tiles, fauna, environment) with the planet's own name, seed and look. Every generated planet
  and moon is landable (main._build_system; request_land/land_on use get_planet).
- Stations and asteroid fields stay exactly where they were (Galaxy._old_planet_draws replays the old
  generator's random draws; checked against the old galaxy.gd: 0 of 38 stations moved).
- Name pools grown to 36+ per empire (3 systems x 12) with more real places.
- Galaxy page: "N planets · M moons"; system map: moons named only when zoomed in enough to separate
  them from their planet, and without the LAND tag (it overlapped).
Numbers: this galaxy: 93 planets + 58 moons across 15 generated systems (Lukka: 12 planets, 10 moons).
Tests: test_galaxy test_generated_planets, test_land_on_generated_planets (an ice planet + a moon land and
build); test_system_star_and_planet_names allows moons. 181 pass.
Not yet: FPS tour check (the machine was busy) - big systems have up to ~22 orbiting bodies.
Files: scripts/galaxy.gd, scripts/planet_data.gd, scripts/main.gd, scripts/pages/galaxy_page.gd,
scripts/pages/map_page.gd, tests/test_galaxy.gd, data/docs/game.md.

## 2026-11-11 - Commodities market, trade routes on the maps, keyboard / gamepad controls
Asked: make the station market a proper trading terminal; show trade routes on the system and galaxy
maps; WASD navigation in menus; shortcuts easy to change in Settings; start gamepad support.
Done:
- **Market** (new scripts/pages/market_page.gd, MarketPage; station_menu.gd's MARKET tab): a table of
  every good grouped by category (Foods, Medicines, Machinery, Technology, Energy, Consumer goods,
  Weapons, Minerals, Salvage) with columns SELL / BUY / GALACTIC AVG (+ how far this station's price is
  from it, green up / red down) / SUPPLY (bars + stock) / DEMAND (bars, goods the station uses) / CARGO;
  the selected good lit amber. Right panel: the good's prices, a quantity picker (- / + / MAX, A/D,
  Shift: 10), BUY / SELL, and the best prices within 2 jumps with the profit a unit and a plot-route
  button. Keys: W/S (arrows, D-pad) select, A/D quantity, Enter / pad A buy, Backspace / pad X sell.
  Replaced the old list of rows with 4 buttons each (Buy 1 / Buy 10 / Sell 1 / Sell all).
- **TradeRoutes** (new scripts/trade_routes.gd): a price table of every station x every good (built
  at most once a second - prices move every 2 s economy tick), galactic averages, supply / demand bars,
  route search (from stations, within N jumps over the gate lanes, best destination per station+good,
  never to systems hostile to you), galaxy_routes (best run per system pair), drawing (glowing line,
  chevrons streaming along it, arrowhead, a tag "GOOD +profit" placed clear of other tags).
- **Galaxy map** (galaxy_page.gd): TRADE ROUTES toggle (cart button, T) + a goods filter (all / one);
  the ten best runs between systems drawn along the gate lanes (side by side on shared lanes, the best
  brightest); the right column lists them instead of diplomacy / news - click one to plot a route to
  where you buy. Refreshed every 2 s.
- **Sector map** (map_page.gd): TRADE toggle (T): runs from this system's charted stations - to another
  station here, or to the gate toward a station up to 2 jumps away ("> SPARTA" on the tag).
- **Keybinds** (new autoload scripts/keybinds.gd): 30 actions in 3 groups (Menus, Flight, Toolbar), each
  2 keys + 1 gamepad input, registered in the InputMap, saved to user://keybinds.cfg (only what differs
  from the defaults); pad A / B join ui_accept / ui_cancel. Menu navigation: registered menus (station,
  Ship Computer, Field Computer, title / pause menu) - WASD / arrows / D-pad / left stick move the focus
  (the first press focuses the first button), Q / R or LB / RB switch tabs (cycle_tab). Gameplay keys in
  main.gd, planet_surface.gd, ship_menu.gd, field_menu.gd, station_menu.gd, surface_map.gd go through it

- **Settings > Controls** (main_menu.gd): a page listing every action with KEY / ALT KEY / GAMEPAD
  buttons - click one and press the key / pad input (Esc cancels), right-click clears, red = used twice
  in a group, a reset per action and Reset all; the connected gamepad's name on the settings page.
- **Gamepad** (start): left stick flies the ship (toward a point ahead; let go: stop) and walks the pilot
  on planets; RT attacks the nearest enemy (a trigger counts once per pull); LB / RB previous / next
  weapon in flight; Y dock / undock; Back Ship Computer; Start pause; B closes the Ship Computer / maps.
- Guide (data/docs/game.md): market, sector map, galaxy, controls (menus, gamepad, rebinding).

## 2026-11-11 - Tabs on Q / E, undock on Shift + D

## 2026-11-11 - Independents, mixed station ownership, reputation in place of merits
Asked: ships and stations belonging to no empire are independent - neutral with everyone, out of every
conflict. Most stations in a system belong to the empire occupying it, but empires at war, expanding or
allied can bring their own (an ally by the owner's leave, or while conquering it). The player is friend
or foe of an empire only through reputation - missions and trade raise it; it falls, slowly, only when
attacking NPCs. A reputation system for it; the merit system no longer needed.
Done:
- **Independents** (galaxy.gd EMPIRES "independent", not a major power): never at war with any empire
  (at_war), only the Sea Peoples prey on them; their own reputation; station designs (halo / wheel /
  gateway). A quarter of the civilian ships met are independent (main.gd spawn_ship; never patrols);
  traders from independent ports are independent.
- **Station ownership per station** (station record "empire", station_owner(), station_presence():
  "" / independent / outpost / forward): the occupying empire always runs the majority (_room_for_guest:
  guests fewer than the owner's stations, at most 2). At the start (_generate_guests, a separate random
  stream: the owner's stations, planets and fields unchanged): an independent free port in most systems
  ("Rhodos Free Port", "Lemnos Waystation"... - Aegean islands + Free Port / Waystation / Exchange /
  Freehold / Caravanserai / Commons), and an ally next door may keep an outpost (Mycenaean "Orestes Lion
  Gate" in Sparta). During play (_guests_tick, with the diplomacy tick): an ally bordering a system may
  be granted an outpost; an empire at war bordering it may set up a forward base (news); forward bases
  undermine the system's control from inside (_control_cycle, 6-12 a cycle); an outpost of an empire no
  longer welcome (relation < 20, at peace) declares itself independent; when a system falls (border
  battle or control cycle) the loser's stations there go to the winner (_transfer). Saved: runtime-added
  stations (rebuilt in order) and every station's owner.
- **Reputation** (REP_TIERS): Hostile < -50 (warships attack, docking refused) / Unfriendly < -15 /
  Neutral / Cordial 15 / Friendly 40 / Allied 70; standing(), tier changes are news. Rises: missions
  (mission tiers now on the same thresholds - Routine from Unfriendly, Trusted Cordial, Honoured
  Friendly, Hero Allied), trade at their stations (1 per 1,000 cr bought or sold), pirate kills in their
  space (+2). Falls: first shot at one of their ships -2 (once a ship, enemy.gd), each destroyed -8
  (was -20: now ~6 ships to turn an empire hostile, was 2), a civilian shot down in another empire's
  space -2 with that empire; war enemies of the victim +2. A bad name fades +1 a minute toward 0.
  Effects: market prices by standing with the station's owner (Hostile +15% / Unfriendly +10% ... Allied
  -10% buying, sell prices the other way), bounties +10% Friendly / +25% Allied with the system's owner.
- **Removed**: pledge, merits, ranks (Recruit-Archon), empire missions (fortify / undermine / secure),
  pledge discounts and rank bounty bonus; the station's EMPIRE tab is now REPUTATION (who runs this
  station and what it is, the system's holder, control and attackers; your standing with every empire
  and the independents - a bar, tier and its effects; how it moves). Scenario condition "pledged" ->
  "standing" (at least a tier with an empire); themes rule "pledge" -> "friends" (Friendly+ empires).
- Maps: the galaxy page's station list names guests (", Mycenaean allied outpost", ", independent"),
  Independents in the legend and the diplomacy list; the sector map shows guest stations in their
  owner's colour with what they are; hover shows owner and your standing. Station header: owner,
  presence, your standing.
- Guide (empire page rewritten, bounties), tutorial page, editor docs (themes, scenarios).

  story's) + Keros, the Cycladic heart, then each empire spreads outward from its territory (away from
  the middle) to EMPIRE_SIZE systems: Minoa 9, Athens 10, Sparta 8 (hemmed in; 9 wanted), Mycenae 8,
  Ionia 10, Cyclades 8, Sea Peoples 5 - 58 systems, 88 gate lanes. Each new system 100+ from any other,
  its lane to its parent crossing no lane, plus one more lane to a near neighbour where it can (loops,
  contested borders); named from SYSTEM_NAMES (the empire's further cities and islands, never another
  name in use). SYSTEMS / LINKS are now static vars built once. 177 stations, 625 planets.

  ("Eleusis Beta"); planet surface seeds unique (_unique_seed: the same draw, a repeat moves on).

  tick and after your trades; cache_prices: one price() a good) - TradeRoutes.table 36 ms -> 1.3 ms;
  galaxy_routes 138 ms -> ~10 ms (each system's best seller per good, then the best within reach, then
  the best run per system pair; reach cached; results cached 2 s); the economy spread over twice the
  frames (ECO_PER_FRAME 3); traders 42 -> 110. The galaxy map's still layers (back: grid, stars,
  territories, lanes; top: badges, names, route, legend) drawn into two SubViewports re-rendered only
  when they change, the dashed lanes in one draw_multiline, stars and territories one texture -
  draw calls 1589 -> 246 (232 -> 476 fps); the map's view idles while hidden.

## 2026-11-11 - War fleets, sieges, burning and destroyed stations, trade routes you know of
Asked: fleets of 3-12 ships that protect systems and/or invade others, attacking the stations of
empires at war; flames on a severely damaged station, which then offers only repair-resource and
station-defence missions; attacking an empire's ships lowers relations, repairs only raise them; a
station at zero health is destroyed completely; trade routes only between discovered and visited
stations, and being Friendly with an empire reveals all its trade routes.
Done:
- **Fleets** (new autoload scripts/fleets.gd): each empire keeps defence fleets (one per 3 systems,
  3-8 ships) and, at war, invasion fleets (6-12) against an enemy system on its border (not the home
  system); fleets move along the lanes (30 s a jump, routes from Galaxy.find_route); away from you,
  every 5 s: enemy fleets in a system trade losses by strength, an invasion with no defenders wears down
  the stations of the empires it's at war with (SIEGE_DAMAGE 0.6 a ship a tick; stations shoot back),
  then captures the system when its owner has no station left there; defenders go to the help of a
  besieged system within 3 jumps; a peace turns invasions into defenders bound home; stations mend
  0.4 a tick when not besieged. News for gatherings, arrivals, battles, burning, destruction, conquest.
  Saved with the galaxy.
- **Live** (main.gd): the system's fleets are real ships (_spawn_fleet: defenders about the system,
  invaders round their target station; arriving fleets come in at a gate - fleet_arrived); each ship
  knows its fleet (enemy.gd fleet_id, saved) - a loss counts (Fleets.ship_lost), and isn't respawned as
  a patrol; invaders' siege_target - the station they shoot when no enemy ship is near, the next most
  damaged one when it falls; a besieged station's safe zone protects nobody (station.under_attack).
  The old "two raiders from a warring neighbour" spawn is replaced by the fleets; 2 militia remain.
- **Stations** (station.gd): condition = the Galaxy record's health (0-100; HIT_POINTS 25 damage a
  point); hit by bolts like a ship (your shots at one: -0.5 standing a hit); below Galaxy.DAMAGED (40)
  it burns: fires at spots across it (by its id, turning with it) - rising tongues of flame, a
  flickering hot core, drifting smoke, more and bigger the worse it is (one texture: they batch); at 0
  a chain of explosions and gone (Galaxy.destroy_station: out of the galaxy for good, saved; traders
  bound there re-routed; ids from a per-system counter so none is reused). The home system's stations
  can burn but never fall below 10 (the story's). Station header: condition, BURNING.
- **Crisis missions** (missions.gd): a burning station offers only "Repairs: <material>" (bring N
  machinery / iron or titanium ore / energy cells / electronics; turned in it mends 6 + 1.2 a unit %,
  and the mission's reputation) and "Defend <station>" (destroy N warships of a besieging empire in its
  system; counted from your kills - empire warships now count for missions) - the Missions tab says why.
- **Trade routes you know** (galaxy.gd visited / seen / knowledge; trade_routes.gd): a route starts at a
  station whose market you know (docked there - visit_station - or its owner is Friendly / Allied with
  you) and ends at one you've found (within sensor range - see_station - or docked, or Friendly);
  applies to the galaxy map, the sector map and the Market's best prices; caches follow `knowledge`.
- Guide (empires page: fleets and invasions, damaged stations; market: routes you know).
Numbers: ~25 fleets at the start (defence) + invasions at war; a 10-ship siege burns a healthy station in
~1.5 min. FPS: new scenario "space: a siege, a burning station" 416 fps (p95 3.3 ms); space tour 28/28
at 240+. Tests: new tests/test_war.gd (fleets staffed 3-12, every empire defends; an invasion burns,
destroys and captures, kept in the save; crisis missions only, repairs mend and raise standing, defence
counts the besieger's ships only; routes only from known markets to found stations, Friendly shares);
test_trade updated; full suite 205.

## 2026-11-11 - More realistic station fires

Asked: "more realistic flames" (the burning-station fires looked like glowing yellow blobs).

Done (scripts/station.gd, _draw_fire / _draw_flames / fire_texture):
- A new fire texture made once at startup (SpaceStation.fire_texture, 256 x 128): a soft round puff and a tongue of flame (wide, round base, tapering to a wavering point), both on one texture so every fire draw batches. The old ExhaustTrail.disc was hard-edged, which is why the fires looked like blobs.
- Each fire site: a charred scorch on the hull; 8 smoke puffs billowing up, swelling, drifting with a slow wind and fading from dark to pale grey; an outer body of 10 red-orange tongues and an inner one of 7 yellow ones, each rising, stretching, swaying and cooling darker as it fades (normal blending, so they cover the bright hulls).
- An additive child layer (_fire_layer, CanvasItemMaterial ADD) carries the light: a heat glow on the hull, a white-hot heart and flickering embers. It is created when the station starts burning and freed when it's mended.
- Fewer but bigger fires: 3 to 7 sites (was 5 to 11), each 0.16 to 0.24 of the radius (was 0.07 to 0.12).

Files: scripts/station.gd.
